title: Discovering West Africa: Ghana, Senegal, Cameroon
description:
S01 E01 — Made in Ghana
Ghana is blessed with a vibrant culture and a scenic coastline.

title: Discovering West Africa: Ghana, Senegal, Cameroon
description:
S01 E02 — Ghanaian Botanical Gardens, Afropop, and Yoga
To fully experience Ghana, explorers must spend time with local musicians and take a nature hike.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E01 — Exploring the Gift of the Nile
For the ancient Egyptians, the Nile is the source of all life; Egypt's ancient cities and monuments; the rich pantheon of Egyptian gods; the role of Egyptian kings as divine intermediaries; the symbolism of Egyptian architecture, art and ritual.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E02 — The Major Museums of Cairo
Using objects from Cairo's three great museums; tracing 5,000 years of Egyptian history; Narmer Palette sets the conventions for Egyptian art; what a statue of King Khafre and Tutankhamun's golden throne tell about Egypt from various periods.

title: Experiencing America: A Smithsonian Tour through American History
description:
S01 E01 — Star-Spangled Banner - Inspiring the Anthem
A tour of national treasures from the Smithsonian; the artifact that inspires the national anthem; the flag that flows over Fort McHenry when Francis Scott Key pens "The Star-Spangled Banner"; the battle for the fort and the history of the flag.

title: Experiencing America: A Smithsonian Tour through American History
description:
S01 E02 — Presidents and Generals - Images of Leadership
How some of the country's greatest leaders have seen themselves and been seen by the nation; Washington's uniform, swords and portraits; notable photographs of Lincoln; the history of Eisenhower's distinctive army jacket and his presidential look.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E01 — George Washington's Doubts
Explaining the importance of getting a well-rounded understanding of the Founders; Professor Guelzo explores Washington's fears about post-Revolutionary America; Washington's concerns about how people could administer their own affairs.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E02 — Thomas Mifflin's Congress
Before the ratification of the Constitution, there are presidents of the Congress created by the Articles of Confederation; the failures of one president, Thomas Mifflin, offer a window into the problems facing the United States of America in 1783.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E01 — The Many Faces of Jesus
Scholars who have devoted their lives to studying the ancient sources about Jesus come to varying conclusions; seeing what can be learned about what Jesus most likely says and does by working from a strictly historical perspective.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E02 — One Remarkable Life
Beginning the study of the historical Jesus by examining the world within which the Christian religion is born; this world is largely populated by "pagans" who, unlike the Jews and then later the Christians, believe not in one but in many gods.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E01 — America's Founding Ideas
Start the course on the U.S. Constitution by learning about the English culture that inspired American law and the conflict with England that caused the revolution.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E02 — Failures of Early American Governments
Consider where the Articles of Confederation came from.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E01 — What Does It Mean to Be Human?
Exploring human development and the considering questions about early life.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E02 — Stones and Bones: The First Fossil Families
Homo habilis, the earliest known species of the genus.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E01 — A Tale of Two Ancient Cities
Jericho and Anau are two of the world's oldest cities; their stories have much to say about the scope of human history; what makes these cities successful; how they differ from each other; introducing the concept and key themes of Big History.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of Humanity
Tracing the origins of the human species from the emergence of proto-humans to the rise of Homo sapiens, Professor Benjamin offers perspectives to show what makes the human species unique and why it has been able to flourish.

title: Discovering West Africa: Ghana, Senegal, Cameroon
description:
S01 E01 — Made in Ghana
Ghana is blessed with a vibrant culture and a scenic coastline.

title: Discovering West Africa: Ghana, Senegal, Cameroon

To fully experience Ghana, explorers must spend time with local musicians and take a nature hike.

description:
S01 E02 — Presidents and Generals - Images of Leadership
How some of the country's greatest leaders have seen themselves and been seen by the nation; Washington's uniform, swords and portraits; notable photographs of Lincoln; the history of Eisenhower's distinctive army jacket and his presidential look.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Birth of Christianity
This lecture introduces some issues essential to understanding how Christianity begins; growing away from its Jewish roots; ultimately becoming the most important religion of the civilization.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — The Religious World of Early Christianity
This lecture introduces the pagan, polytheistic religions that dominate the early world; the most important Roman religion for the birth of Christianity; Judaism, the religion of Jesus and his followers.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — The Historical Jesus
In the first of three lectures on the birth of Christianity, Professor Ehrman examines the life of Jesus of Nazareth; referred to both outside the New Testament and within the Gospels themselves.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Oral and Written Traditions about Jesus
How four anonymous authors who live decades after Jesus record traditions that have been circulating orally over the intervening years; examining the extent to which those traditions have been modified in the retelling.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E01 — The Historical Study of Christianity
The historical trajectory of Christianity; contemporary ignorance of its past; considering the value of the historical study of Christianity; looking at the methods and role of the historian; the sources and limitations of historical knowledge.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E02 — The First Cultural Context - Greece and Rome
Investigating the culture of the Mediterranean world in which Christianity is born; the legacy of Alexander; the features of Greek politics, religion and philosophy; learning about the nature of Roman rule and imperial order in the region.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E03 — The First Cultural Context - Judaism
The circumstances of Jewish life in ancient Palestine and the diaspora; examining cultural and ideological factors that divide the Jews; the tensions they face between assimilation and separation; their resistance to Greek culture and Roman rule.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E04 — The Jesus Movement and the Birth of Christianity
Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E05 — Paul and Christianity's First Expansion
Observing how Christianity's expansion happens; the broad adaptations it makes in a relatively short period; investigating the role of Paul's letters as a primary record of the convictions, culture, practices and troubles of the early Christians.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E06 — The Diversity of Early Christianity
Influences in early Christianity beyond Jesus and Paul; the differences in conviction and perspective in the gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John; the four Gospels' interpretations of Jesus's role; their convergence on the nature of his character.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E01 — The Many Faces of Jesus
Scholars who have devoted their lives to studying the ancient sources about Jesus come to varying conclusions; seeing what can be learned about what Jesus most likely says and does by working from a strictly historical perspective.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E02 — One Remarkable Life
Beginning the study of the historical Jesus by examining the world within which the Christian religion is born; this world is largely populated by "pagans" who, unlike the Jews and then later the Christians, believe not in one but in many gods.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E03 — Scholars Look at the Gospels
The work of German writer D. F. Strauss argues that the Gospels are best understood as containing history-like stories that intend to convey truth but do not occur as they are narrated, which is why most scholars find his approach illuminating.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E04 — Fact and Fiction in the Gospels
Scholars question the historical accuracy of some gospel accounts not out of hostility toward Christianity, but because of historical evidence; what this evidence is; how historians assess it.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E05 — The Birth of the Gospels
Before the Gospels, accounts of Jesus are passed on by word of mouth; whether it is possible to move "behind" the written accounts to learn more about this original oral tradition, and perhaps even about Jesus himself as a historical person.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E06 — Some of the Other Gospels
In addition to the New Testament, other written sources about Jesus come down from antiquity; what these other, noncanonical Gospels are like; considering their origins and sources; how much they can reveal about what Jesus actually says and does.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E01 — Needing No Introduction?
Mark Twain is a celebrity of almost mythic status; explaining the origin of Samuel Clemens's famous pseudonym; asking what Mark Twain means to his American audience and to the man who creates him.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E02 — From Samuel Clemens to Mark Twain
Seeing Twain's life as one of milestones; the financial success brought by his literary triumphs is at times disrupted by disastrous investments such as the Paige typesetting machine; Twain's happy married life is hit by several family tragedies.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E03 — The Sense of Mark Twain's Humor
Twain says that as a humorist, "I have always preached."; his sermon consists of "cracking up" idols of reverence to make room for truth; his speech about the "cannibals" of the Sandwich Islands shows him tickling the audience's funny bones.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E04 — Marketing Twain
Concerning his writing, Twain once confesses that the motive of profit has an importance "almost beyond my own comprehension."; exploring why money means so much to Twain; detailing the marketing schemes he uses to maximize his income.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E05 — Innocents Abroad, I-Going East
Henry Ward Beecher organizes Twain's trip East as a pilgrimage to pay obeisance to the founding monuments of Western culture; how Twain turns the tables; whether Twain is psychologically preparing America for its role as a world power.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E06 — Innocents Abroad, II-Traveling to Unlearn
Twain's goal in "Innocents Abroad" is to teach his readers to see the Old World with their own eyes, asking what of value can remain after everything is mocked into submission when Twain trains his wit on the holy sites of the Bible.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E07 — Roughing It-Going West
Twain mines his own past as a prospector and turns it into comic frontier fiction in "Roughing It"; the work also marks Twain's first prominent use of American vernacular language; his intimation that it deserves a place in American literature.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E08 — The Lecture Tours
Despite the rigors of touring and the limitations imposed by his audiences' tastes, Twain comes to love the thrill of live lecturing; he skillfully blends the serious academic content that audiences demand with his own trademark sardonic wit.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E01 — Meeting the Norse Gods of the Viking Age
The Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda chronicle the lives of the Norse gods of the Viking Age.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E02 — Fate and the Norse Worldview
Insight into the profound Norse sense of fatalism and the importance of reckless courage.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E03 — The Norse Art of Mythic Storytelling
A comparison of two versions of a story to highlight the dream logic inherent to Norse mythology.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E04 — The Norse Gods Are Characters with Flaws
An in-depth understanding of different shades of the personalities of the Norse gods.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E05 — The Norse Creation: Dawn of Strife
Discovering how the Norse creation myth begins and ends.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E06 — First Humans, the Nine Realms, and Yggdrasil
A broader look at the Norse mythos and humanity's place within it.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E07 — Loki and His Children
The story of Loki, a complicated figure who lives alongside the gods but compulsively troubles them.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E08 — Balder's Death: Tragic Murder of a God
One of the two different versions of the story of Balder's death omits the presence of Loki.

S01 E05 — The Norse Creation: Dawn of Strife
Discovering how the Norse creation myth begins and ends.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E06 — First Humans, the Nine Realms, and Yggdrasil
A broader look at the Norse mythos and humanity's place within it.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E07 — Loki and His Children
The story of Loki, a complicated figure who lives alongside the gods but compulsively troubles them.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E08 — Balder's Death: Tragic Murder of a God
One of the two different versions of the story of Balder's death omits the presence of Loki.

title: King Arthur: History and Legend
description:
S01 E01 — The Origins of King Arthur
Studying images of the Arthurian legend and their relationship to historical reality; tracing the history of post-Roman Britain; the large-scale invasions of the Anglo-Saxons; evidence that a single individual rose up to lead his people.

title: King Arthur: History and Legend
description:
S01 E02 — An Arthur-Like Figure in Cornwall
Investigating archeological and historical evidence that supports the existence of an Arthur-like figure in early Britain; studying the site of Cadbury Castle, the center of operations of a leader who thwarted the Saxons; the supposed tomb of Arthur.

title: King Arthur: History and Legend
description:
S01 E03 — King Arthur in the Latin Chronicles
Exploring some of the most significant early witnesses to the Arthurian legend; studying accounts of Arthur's exploits and death in Latin texts and the Welsh Annales Cambriae; how texts from the 11th and 12th century C.E. embellished the legend.

title: King Arthur: History and Legend
description:
S01 E04 — King Arthur in Wales - The Mabinogion
How Arthur became a cultural touchstone in early Welsh history; key references to the Arthurian saga in the Black Book of Carmarthen and the Triads of the Island of Britain; the portrayal of Arthur in the tales of the Mabinogion.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E01 — Who Are the Celts?
Examining and clarifying common preconceptions about Celtic identity; painting the initial brushstrokes on the canvas of a European culture most widely perceived as Scottish and Irish while promising much more.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E02 — The Celts and the Classical World
Studying the earliest written records of the Celts from Italy, Greece and Spain, dating as far back as the sixth century B.C.; scholarly theories about the Celts' migration throughout Europe; the foundation of humanity's understanding of the Celts.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E03 — Celtic Art and Artifacts
How archeological studies of Celtic artifacts have woven a rich tapestry of their millennia-old society; learning about war trumpets, gold necklaces and other recovered objects from around Europe; building an image of this ever-adapting culture.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E04 — Celtic Languages in the Ancient World
The discovery of Celtic inscriptions on Spain's western coast; the possibility of a common language along maritime trade routes; revolutionizing studies of Celtic origins and migration; the long-standing theory of Central European Celtic origins.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E01 — Julia Disobeys Emperor Augustus
The experiences of Julia, the daughter of Caesar Augustus; a window into the way many pre-modern societies sought to control morality; Julia's life of thwarted potential; understanding what women had to overcome to make a mark on history.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E02 — Herodias Has John the Baptist Beheaded
The portrayal of the John the Baptist's death as the whim of the young femme fatale Salome; why the truth is much more complicated; the story of Salome's mother, Herodias; how Herodias's hunger for power and recognition left her exiled and forgotten.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E03 — The Trung Sisters of Vietnam Fight the Han
China under the Han Dynasty; how imperial expansion threatened the matriarchal culture of Vietnam; the Trung sisters; leading tribal armies against the invaders; how the Trung sisters' story has become a touchstone of Vietnamese culture.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E04 — Boudicca Attacks the Romans
The end of Iron Age Britain and the birth of Roman Britain; the valiant but thwarted rebellion of the Celtic warrior queen, Boudicca; how Boudicca was motivated by personal tragedy; the revival of Boudicca's legacy by Queen Victoria.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E01 — What is a Pirate?
Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E02 — Pirate Facts and Fictions
Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E03 — Real Pirates of the Caribbean
How the Spanish's power hold on the Caribbean is broken; which nationalities join in the free-for-all; the historical importance of Alexander Exquemelin's "Buccaneers of America" and Captain Charles Johnson's "A General History of the Pyrates".

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E04 — Pirate Attacks and Tactics
Pirates want money or anything they can turn into money; consequently, they usually wish for a speedy surrender, do not want a battle and rarely sink captured ships; the many tactics pirates use to apprehend their prey in the age of sails.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E01 — The Colonists as Faithful Subjects
In pamphlets and pulpits of the colonies, one is reminded of the close, even familial ties extending across an ocean, strengthened by customs and values shaped over centuries.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E02 — Colonial Constitutions and Their Inspiration
Trade between colonies and with Great Britain and other nations call for orderly procedures, as does the governance of growing communities and steady influx of immigrants.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E03 — Who ``Founded'' the United States?
As colonial constitutions are fashioned, the context within which deliberations and strategies are conducted is that of the Enlightenment; the United States is founded as much by ideas as by men.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E04 — Taxation Without Representation
The colonies return to the crown, over a period of years, revenues exceeding what was expected; the Stamp Act; why 10 tons of Darjeeling are sent to the bottom of Boston Harbor.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E05 — The Declaration of Independence
This document is the first of its kind; one that announces the creation of a new nation and the need to provide reasons for this precipitous measure; it is a veritable text on the manner in which political issues are to be understood.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E06 — The Royalist View of the Revolution
In the colonies and Great Britain, the American Revolution is cast as a rebellion against the rule of law; this sheds light on colonial debates on political authority.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E07 — The Articles of Confederation
The articles are the product of danger and emergency; principles for joint action among the colonies for the express purpose of waging a war of independence.

title: American Ideals: Founding a Republic of Virtue
description:
S01 E08 — The Constitution of the United States, Part 1
In the brutally hot Philadelphia months, a diverse and argumentative assembly meets for unclear purposes.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E01 — Benjamin Franklin and the American Dream
In Franklin's unfinished autobiography, he creates a persona for himself as a role model others may follow; there is more to Franklin than he shows on the page; surveying the book offers some foundational insights into his life and his worldview.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E02 — Meet the Franklins
The Franklins are a typical 18th-century family, extended across space; filled with comedy and tragedy, wealth and poverty; meeting his parents and siblings; learning the story of his wife and firstborn son; accompanying Franklin on his travels.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E03 — Benjamin Franklin's Boston Beginnings
One may associate Franklin with Philadelphia, but his roots lie in Boston; many of the virtues Franklin cultivates throughout his life grow from the values of the Boston Puritans; witnessing the events that Franklin experiences in his youth.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E04 — Benjamin Franklin and Philadelphia
Shifting attention to the City of Brotherly Love; 18th-century Philadelphia is one of the leading cities in British America; it is one of the leading cities in the British Empire; what makes this city so important; how the city shapes Franklin.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E05 — Benjamin Franklin in London
If Philadelphia is one of the British Empire's leading cities, London itself becomes the metropolis of the Western world, the largest city in Europe and the nexus of global trade; getting to know this city; examining some of Franklin's pastimes.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E06 — Benjamin Franklin: Printer and Postmaster
A major revolution in the 18th century thanks to the printing press; the rise in literacy, the spread of ideas and the creation of communities across oceans reshapes the world's intellectual landscape; delving into Franklin's career as a printer.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E07 — Benjamin Franklin: Scientist
The 18th century sees scientific paradigms shift; Franklin is a scientist, or as he would term it, a "natural philosopher"; his scientific contributions would earn him a place in the history books; examining some of his major inventions and ideas.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E08 — Benjamin Franklin and Electricity
Unpacking Franklin's greatest scientific contributions, which are in the field of electricity; reviewing his most important discoveries, experiments and contributions; reflecting on the lasting legacy of Franklin as a scientist.
